Information Minister Neth Pheaktra confirmed their arrival, while the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) monitored the handover, which had been briefly delayed by Thai accusations of drone violations by Cambodia.

The center emphasized that the move does not impact Thai sovereignty and was not part of any secret exchange or conditions.

titleEn: Cambodia demands Thailand withdraw all military personnel and equipment from Cambodian territory to legally recognized border locations

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona clarified that unilateral Thai actions like placing containers or raising flags do not constitute legal evidence of a border. Maly Socheata added that the military is monitoring the ceasefire implementation by the Thai side, noting it is a shared responsibility.
title: Cambodia Reaffirms Official Border with Thailand, Rejects Unilateral Actions

summary: Thailand's Second Army Region released video footage allegedly showing Cambodian forces using the Preah Vihear temple site as a military base and weapons cache. The report claims anti-tank rockets similar to those seized in previous clashes were spotted. Officials noted that while the situation is under control, the military remains on high alert for any escalation.
title: Army Region 2 Releases Video of Cambodian Buildup at Preah Vihear

summary: Cambodia's Information Minister Neth Pheaktra told AFP that the Thai military has begun an 'illegal annexation' of territory, specifically Chouk Chey village. Reports state Thai forces have installed barbed wire and shipping containers to create a border fence. Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul countered these claims while visiting troops in Surin, stating Thailand has never breached sovereignty and acts in accordance with international regulations.
title: Cambodia accuses Thailand of ‘annexing’ border village

summary: Cambodia formally called on Thailand on Saturday to withdraw all military personnel and equipment from areas Phnom Penh claims as its own. This demand comes exactly one week after a December 27 truce halted three weeks of deadly clashes. The Cambodian foreign ministry specifically cited the seizure of areas across four border provinces during the conflict. The Thai army has rejected these claims, stating their forces are in areas that have 'always belonged to Thailand.'
title: Cambodia demands Thailand withdraw troops, week into border truce

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated in a press conference that Cambodia does not recognize any border changes resulting from the use of force. He detailed specific Thai actions during the ceasefire, including placing shipping containers, spreading barbed wire, and planting Thai national flags on Cambodian soil. He urged citizens to trust the government's peaceful and legal resolution efforts.
title: Cambodia: Thailand has spread barbed wire, planted flags, destroyed Cambodian homes – acts that violate Cambodia’s territorial integrity, agreed agreements, UN Charter
titleEn: Cambodia: Thailand has spread barbed wire, planted flags, destroyed Cambodian homes

summary: The Thai First Army Region has urged citizens to stop sharing videos of seized assets or posts mocking the opposing side. Military officials expressed concern that such content could be used as evidence of human rights violations in international legal forums and damage Thailand's diplomatic standing. The military emphasized that the situation has entered a sensitive phase involving international legal negotiations where social media narratives play a strategic role.
title: The Thailand-Cambodia border war: Thai First Army Region issues warning over social media posts threatening national security

summary: Cambodian authorities repatriated 162 Thai nationals through the Ban Laem permanent border checkpoint in Chanthaburi. The group had been detained in Siem Reap. Initial screenings by Thai authorities found 6 individuals with outstanding warrants, who were taken into custody for legal processing, while others undergo standard screening and assistance procedures.
title: กัมพูชาส่งตัว 162 คนไทยกลับประเทศ หลังถูกกักตัวในเมืองเสียมราฐ
titleEn: Cambodia returns 162 Thais after detention in Siem Reap

summary: The Ministry of Information issued a 5-point directive to social media users and journalists to prevent 'fake news' and AI-generated 'deepfakes' that could incite racial discrimination or anger during border negotiations. It orders the public to rely only on official government sources to support diplomatic efforts for a permanent ceasefire.
title: Cambodia Issues Media Guidelines to Ease Border Tensions With Thailand

summary: Dorna Sports has re-confirmed that Thailand will host the MotoGP 2026 season opener in Buriram from Feb 27 to Mar 1. Organizers had been monitoring the Thai-Cambodian border conflict closely as Buriram is near the border and the Chang International Circuit was briefly used as a temporary shelter. Authorities assured that the situation is easing and will not affect the event.
title: ดอร์น่า สปอร์ต ยืนยัน ประเทศไทยสนามเปิดโมโตจีพี 2026 หลังจับตาดูสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย – กัมพูชา
titleEn: Dorna Sports confirms Thailand as 2026 MotoGP opener after monitoring border situation

summary: This report frames the Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs' protest as a reaction to military loss. Cambodia claims Thailand is illegally occupying areas in Banteay Meanchey, Pursat, Preah Vihear, and Oddar Meanchey provinces, violating the ceasefire and the Geneva Convention. The Thai source uses highly emotional and biased language.
title: รบแพ้แล้วโวย! กต.เขมรออกแถลงการณ์อ้างไทยยึดครองดินแดนกัมพูชา 4 จังหวัด ผิดกฎหมายระหว่างประเทศ
titleEn: Complaining After Losing! Cambodian MFA Issues Statement Claiming Thailand Illegally Occupies 4 Provinces

summary: Phnom Penh has formally called on Thailand to withdraw its forces from disputed areas, alleging that Thai troops moved into Cambodian territory during the 72-hour ceasefire agreed upon on December 27, 2025. The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs demanded the removal of all military personnel and equipment to positions consistent with the legally established boundary. Meanwhile, the Thai army has rejected claims of seizure, maintaining their presence is within long-standing Thai territory.
title: Cambodia demands Thailand withdraw troops, a week into border truce

summary: Official government news agency AKP reports that Thai forces have used excavators to level homes and erected shipping containers and barbed wire in the Boeung Trakuon area of Banteay Meanchey province. Governor Oum Reatrey stated this occupation occurred after the Dec 27 ceasefire, displacing over 6,000 people and destroying 1,365 homes.
title: Cambodia Accuses Thai Military of Breaching Ceasefire, Seizing Border Territory

summary: The Second Army Region described the border situation as a 'tactical ceasefire' where large-scale clashes have stopped but military preparations continue. Reports indicate Cambodia is repairing bunkers and using drones for surveillance, while Thai forces remain on high alert for landmines and unauthorized UAV flights in provinces like Ubon Ratchathani and Sisaket.
title: Army Region 2: Tactical Ceasefire Holds Despite Persistent Tensions

summary: Cambodia has formally called on Thailand to withdraw military personnel and equipment from areas it claims are within its territory, one week after a ceasefire halted the worst fighting in over a decade. The Cambodian Foreign Ministry released a statement demanding a return to 'legally established' boundaries, accusing Thai forces of seizing several areas across four provinces during the December conflict.
title: Cambodia demands Thailand withdraw troops

summary: The border situation remains 'operationally quiet but security-tense.' In Ubon Ratchathani and Sisaket, no clashes were found, but Cambodian activity includes transporting structures near Preah Vihear and strict bans on photographing military bases. In Buriram, three unexploded ordnances from previous fighting were found near Sai Taku pass.
title: ทภ.2 เผยชายแดนไร้ปะทะ แต่กัมพูชายังเสริมที่มั่น-บินโดรน
titleEn: Army Region 2 Reports No Border Clashes, but Cambodia Continues Fortification and Drone Flights

summary: Army Region 2 reports that the situation is currently in a state of 'operational peace but security tension.' While no heavy weapon clashes occurred recently, Cambodia is observed reinforcing bunkers, moving supplies, and deploying drones for reconnaissance, particularly near Chong Bok and Preah Vihear. Thai forces remain in control of all national territory and are monitoring the situation closely.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 2 สรุป สถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย–กัมพูชา ไร้ปะทะหนัก แต่ยังตรึงกำลัง
titleEn: Army Region 2 Summary: No Heavy Clashes on Thai-Cambodia Border, but Forces Remain Deployed

summary: A recent poll regarding the upcoming 2026 General Election reveals that 53.5% of Bangkok residents consider a party's policy on Thailand-Cambodia relations as a major factor in their decision. About 62.5% of respondents perceive the current relationship as 'conflicting.' The top concern identified by 41.6% of participants is the protection of sovereignty and the prevention of threats to the country, followed by solving the issue of call center scams based in Cambodia.
title: Poll: 53.5% of Bangkok Residents Say Thai-Cambodia Policy Impacts Their Vote

summary: Army spokesperson Major General Winthai Suvaree officially dismissed Cambodian Foreign Ministry claims that Thai forces have seized land in four provinces. The military asserts that all Thai personnel are operating within sovereign Thai territory and that Cambodia's protests are based on a 'misunderstanding' of historical border markers. Thailand claims it is actually Cambodia that has encroached on Thai soil for decades.
title: Thai Army Rejects Cambodian Land Seizure Allegations

summary: Footage and images shared by Fresh News show Thai military personnel erecting barbed wire fences, placing metal shipping containers, and hoisting the Thai national flag in Prey Chan village, Banteay Meanchey province. These actions reportedly occurred today, Sunday, January 4, 2026, despite the previous week's ceasefire.
title: VIDEO & PICTURES: Thailand continuing to ‘block off’ Cambodian sovereign territory

summary: HE Chan Ratana, Undersecretary of State and Acting Spokesperson of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated during a live broadcast that the Thai military is ignoring the ceasefire agreement of December 27, 2025. He alleged that Thai forces continue to occupy territory in four provinces and are destroying civilian infrastructure in areas like Prey Chan and Chouk Chey village.
title: The Royal Government of Cambodia has made the strongest protest against Thailand's violations, including its continued presence and illegal occupation of Cambodian territory

summary: Minister of Information Neth Pheaktra issued a directive on Saturday urging social media users and journalists to use information responsibly. The goal is to prevent the spread of 'fake news' that could hinder diplomatic efforts to resolve the ongoing border conflict with Thailand following the December 27 ceasefire agreement.
title: Cambodia issues media guidelines to ease border tensions with Thailand

summary: The Thai Joint Press Center released 8 points accusing Cambodia of violating international law. Key allegations include violating Thai sovereignty prior to the ceasefire, using civilian areas as military bases (human shields), and launching attacks from populated areas. Thailand urges the international community to verify facts over rhetoric.
title: เปิด 8 ประเด็นชี้แจงเชิงกฎหมาย กรณีการกระทําของฝ่ายกัมพูชา
titleEn: Revealing 8 Legal Clarification Points Regarding Cambodian Actions

summary: Army Region 2 summarized the situation as of January 3, 2026, stating no heavy weapon clashes occurred. The status is an 'operational ceasefire,' though both sides are strengthening positions. Cambodia is reported to be repairing bunkers, moving supplies, and increasing information security measures.
title: ทภ.2 ชี้ชายแดนไทย–กัมพูชา ยังหยุดยิงเชิงยุทธการ คุมพื้นที่เข้ม เฝ้าระวังภัยแฝง
titleEn: Army Region 2: Thai-Cambodian Border Remains in Operational Ceasefire, Tight Control, Monitoring Hidden Threats

summary: As of Jan 4, the Second Army Region described the border as 'operationally calm but security tense.' While no major clashes were reported that day, surveillance drones from Cambodia were detected in Ubon Ratchathani and Buriram, and Cambodian forces were seen reinforcing bunkers and bunkers near Preah Vihear and Prasat Khna.
title: Border Situation Summary: Tactical Calm but High Tension

summary: The Thai government has leveled serious accusations against the Cambodian military, claiming they committed war crimes and violated international humanitarian law. Specific allegations include establishing military bases and arsenals within civilian areas and discarding the bodies of fallen Cambodian soldiers on the battlefield. Thailand claims to have evidence of Cambodian forces long occupying Thai territory illegally.
title: Thailand accuses Cambodia of war crimes

summary: The Joint Press Center on the Thailand-Cambodia Border Situation issued an official rebuttal to Cambodian claims of territorial encroachment. Thailand reaffirms its respect for sovereignty and international law, stating that it strictly follows the Joint Statement and UN Charter. Thailand remains committed to resolving the border dispute through the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) rather than force.

titleEn: Clarification of Allegations Made by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Cambodia

summary: An international health situation report confirms that since May 2025, the conflict has caused 18 civilian deaths in Cambodia and 16 in Thailand. As of late December, over 490,000 Cambodians (151,000 families) have been displaced, while Thailand also reports extensive evacuations. The report highlights severe economic disruptions, including a sharp drop in remittances and a halt in border trade.
title: Public Health Situation Analysis - Cambodia - Thailand border conflict

summary: China's foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian stated that the late December ceasefire is being gradually implemented. As a key step in the de-escalation process, Thailand has returned 18 Cambodian soldiers who were previously detained. China expressed hope for a 'comprehensive' and 'lasting' truce between the neighbors following the worst border fighting in years.
title: Thailand-Cambodia ceasefire 'gradually' being implemented, says China

summary: Thai cavalry units, specifically the 2nd Cavalry Battalion featuring T-84 Oplot-M tanks, were seen withdrawing from the Ta Phraya area in Sa Kaeo province after completing their assigned mission. Residents were pictured waving flags to thank the departing troops. However, a significant military presence remains stationed along the border to maintain security as local villagers still express distrust toward the Cambodian side despite the ceasefire.
title: “เกาะติดสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย - กัมพูชา” วันที่ 5 ม.ค. 69
titleEn: Monitoring Thailand-Cambodia border situation: Jan 5, 2026

summary: The Thai armed forces issued a statement through the Joint Press Centre on the Thailand–Cambodia Border Situation, urging the international community to assess the situation based on international law and 'verifiable evidence' rather than 'rhetoric.' Thailand rejected claims of territorial seizure, asserting they have evidence that Cambodian forces violated Thai sovereignty prior to the ceasefire by operating in areas under continuous Thai administrative control.
title: Thai military urge international community to verify evidence before accepting Cambodia’s claims

summary: The Thai-Cambodian Border Situation Joint Press Centre issued a statement accusing Cambodia of distorting facts and using provocative language. The Thai side claims these actions violate Articles 14 and 16 of the Joint Statement on the ceasefire, which require both sides to reduce tensions and avoid inflammatory rhetoric. Thailand insists it is acting within its sovereignty and using direct communication channels to resolve disputes.

titleEn: Thai military urges Cambodia to stop provocative communication, violating ceasefire and destroying trust

He described these actions as 'inhumane' and a direct violation of international law and the UN Charter. The government maintains that these unilateral physical markers do not change the legal boundary.
title: Royal Government of Cambodia: Thailand's current actions are an 'internationally illegal act and a violation of the international border line that is unacceptable'

summary: The Chinese foreign ministry stated on Monday that the ceasefire between Thailand and Cambodia is being implemented gradually. Spokesperson Lin Jian confirmed that Thailand has returned 18 captured soldiers to Cambodia as part of the de-escalation efforts. China urged both nations to strive for a comprehensive and lasting peace.
title: Thailand-Cambodia ceasefire ‘gradually’ being implemented, says China

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs informed the international community that between December 7 and 27, 2025, Thai forces launched a pre-planned military offensive across four provinces: Banteay Meanchey, Pursat, Preah Vihear, and Oddar Meanchey. The Ministry claims Thai troops continue to occupy areas deep within Cambodian territory even after the ceasefire, preventing civilians from returning to their homes and violating international humanitarian law.
title: Foreign Ministry: Thai military launched large-scale, systematic operation from Dec 7-27

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul addressed rumors regarding Cambodian military movements near the border. He urged the public to rely on official intelligence from the National Security Council (NSC) rather than social media trends. He declined to confirm if a 'third round' of fighting is imminent, stating he is awaiting a formal briefing. He also noted that while technical-level border committees (JBC) continue to work, high-level signings are paused as the current administration is in a caretaker role.
title: นายกฯ ขออย่าเชื่อกระแสข่าวทหารกัมพูชาเริ่มขยับ เลี่ยงตอบปะทะรอบ 3 รอ สมช.รายงาน
titleEn: PM urges public not to believe rumors of Cambodian troop movements, awaits NSC report on '3rd round' of clashes

summary: The Cambodian State Secretariat of Border Affairs announced that Thailand postponed a JBC meeting scheduled for the first week of January in Siem Reap. Cambodia has countered with a Note Verbale proposing a new meeting for the second or third week of January to discuss demarcation and the recent deployment of Thai containers and flags in disputed areas like O Bei Chorn.
title: Special meeting of the Joint Boundary Commission postponed by Thailand for ‘internal procedures’

summary: Colonel Chainarong Kasee, Commander of Task Force 12, stated that the situation in Sa Kaeo has stabilized. EOD teams have cleared 80-90% of landmines in reclaimed areas near Ban Nong Chan and Ban Nong Ya Kaeo. This has allowed 100% of local residents to return to their homes to survey damages, while the military continues to maintain security along the border line.
title: ผบ.ฉก.12 ยัน ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา สถานการณ์คลี่คลาย ย้ำ ไม่มีความกังวล เดินหน้ารักษาอธิปไตยเต็มกำลัง
titleEn: Task Force 12 Commander Confirms Easing Situation; 100% of Civilians Return to Key Villages

summary: The 2026 academic year has been severely hampered in border areas, with 1,311 schools across seven provinces remaining closed as of late December. According to the Ministry of Education, over 322,000 students and 15,000 teachers are affected. While some schools in Banteay Meanchey and Koh Kong have recently reopened, educational facilities in Preah Vihear remain completely shut due to security risks and infrastructure damage.
title: Border conflict disrupts 2026 school year for 322,000 students

summary: The 1st Army Region clarified that securing border areas in Sa Kaeo using shipping containers and barbed wire is being done within Thai sovereignty for public safety. Demining operations are complete in several villages, allowing residents to return home safely.
title: Army Region 1 updates border management, insists actions are on Thai sovereign land

summary: Army spokesperson Maj. Gen. Winthai Suvaree denied Cambodian protests alleging Thai occupation of land in four provinces. He stated all areas under Thai military control are within Thai territory and are being managed to organize the border efficiently.
title: Thai Army denies land seizure claims, confirms management of sovereign territory

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated on Monday that Thailand will protect its sovereignty and national dignity at all costs. This comes in response to reports that Cambodia might seek international intervention regarding disputed border areas. Anutin emphasized that Thailand will not be at a disadvantage and praised the military for guarding the border during the holiday period.
title: PM Anutin Asserts Right to Protect Sovereignty Against Int'l Intervention

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a 6-point statement accusing Thailand of violating its sovereignty. Key allegations include the illegal occupation of territory in four Cambodian provinces, the destruction of civilian homes, and the use of shipping containers and barbed wire to unilaterally mark borders. Cambodia stated it would not recognize any changes to the boundary resulting from military force.

titleEn: Cambodia Issues 6-Point Statement Claiming Thai Actions Violate International Law; Rejects Border Changes by Force

According to Ministry of Defense reports, while over 25,000 displaced persons have returned home, more than 640,000 Cambodians remain in safety camps. Civil society groups are calling for Thailand to be held accountable for the destruction of civilian property.

titleEn: Residents say Thailand has demolished more than 400 houses in Chouk Chey village and is expanding its invasion into Cambodian territory

summary: Cambodia has issued a Note Verbale re-proposing a special meeting of the Joint Boundary Commission in Siem Reap. The meeting aims to discuss survey work and address allegations of Thai military incursions. This follows a previous postponement by Thailand, which cited internal procedures and landmine concerns.
title: Cambodia re-proposes to Thailand to convene meeting on border demarcation

summary: This analysis contrasts Chinese and U.S. diplomatic efforts. It notes that while U.S. President Donald Trump leveraged tariff threats to push for the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord in October, China held follow-up meetings in Yunnan on Dec 28-29 to consolidate the current ceasefire. The article claims the U.S. approach failed to prevent the December escalation, whereas China's 'Asian Way' focused on rebuilding trust.
title: China demonstrates effective mediation rooted in the 'Asian Way' in Cambodia-Thailand dispute

summary: The Thai Second Army Region accused Cambodian forces of firing a mortar round that injured a Thai sergeant in the Chong Bok area of Ubon Ratchathani on the morning of January 6. Cambodian defense officials, however, described the incident as an accident involving a 'pile of garbage' or an operational error, denying any intent to target Thai territory. The report notes that Thailand has not yet provided specific evidence of the mortar's origin while investigation continues.
title: Thailand accuses Cambodia over mortar incident on Thai soil, no evidence presented

summary: Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has instructed governors of seven provinces bordering Cambodia to remain vigilant despite the lull in fighting. The First Army Region has organized three specific areas in Sa Kaeo province (Ban Klong Phaeng, Ban Nong Chan, and Ban Nong Ya Kaeo) by placing shipping containers and barbed wire to demarcate and secure the boundary. Military engineers are also clearing landmines to allow civilians to return to their homes.

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona reaffirmed Cambodia's stance based on Franco-Siamese treaties and historical maps. He stated that Cambodia does not recognize any boundary alterations resulting from Thai military force. The government also proposed a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting for the second or third week of January in Siem Reap to discuss the unauthorized placement of barbed wire, containers, and bunkers by Thai troops on Cambodian soil.
title: Spokesperson: Cambodia Firmly Defends International Border Established by the Indochina–Siam Boundary Commission and Rejects Any Border Changes by Force

summary: Army Region 2 reported that Cambodian forces fired a mortar round into the Chong Bok area in front of Hill 469 on the morning of January 6. Sgt. Maj. Prachya Philachai sustained shrapnel wounds to his right arm. The Thai military has lodged a formal protest through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, calling it a clear violation of the fragile truce.
title: Cambodia violates ceasefire, shells Chong Bok Hill 469, 1 Thai soldier injured

summary: A Thai soldier was wounded by shrapnel from a Cambodian mortar round fired into Ubon Ratchathani province. The Thai military initially accused Cambodia of violating the December 27 truce, but later stated that Cambodian counterparts claimed the incident was an 'operational error' with no intention to strike Thai territory.
title: Thai Soldier Wounded by Mortar Fire; Cambodia Calls it 'Operational Error'

summary: A 10-day-old truce was broken on Tuesday as a Thai soldier was wounded by shrapnel from mortar rounds fired into Ubon Ratchathani. The report notes that the Dec 27 ceasefire followed nearly three weeks of intense fighting that killed at least 101 people and displaced over half a million. Cambodia has reached out to Thai units to apologize, citing an unintended discharge.
title: Ceasefire violation: Cambodia's 'operational error' breaks 10-day truce; 1 Thai soldier wounded in border clash

One Thai soldier sustained minor shrapnel wounds. Although Cambodia claimed it was an 'operational error,' the Thai Army warned that any future mistakes will force a proportional military retaliation to protect sovereignty.
title: Thai Army Warns Cambodia to Strictly Follow Ceasefire After Mortar Incident

summary: Army Region 2 reported that on the morning of January 6, Cambodian forces fired a mortar round into the Chong Bok area in Nam Yuen District, Ubon Ratchathani. One Thai soldier was injured by shrapnel. While Cambodia later claimed it was an accident during cleaning operations, the Thai military has issued a warning for strict adherence to the ceasefire to prevent future escalations.
title: Army Region 2 confirms Cambodia violated ceasefire with mortar fire at Chong Bok

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that the Thai government is following diplomatic and military protocols following the Jan 6 border incident. He warned that while Thailand currently exercises restraint, the military is prepared to respond proportionally and decisively if the ceasefire is repeatedly violated. The PM emphasized that provincial administrations have been alerted but mass evacuations are not yet required.
title: PM Anutin Warns Cambodia: Thailand Ready to Retaliate if Ceasefire Broken

summary: Local authorities in Banteay Meanchey report that 80 roads, particularly along National Road 58, were severely damaged by Thai artillery and aerial bombing during the conflict from Dec 7–27, 2025. Districts like Ou Chrou and Thmar Puok are heavily affected, with craters making travel difficult. The report also highlights damage to civilian homes, power grids, and water systems.
title: 80 roads in Banteay Meanchey province affected by invasion war and shelling from Thai soldiers

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul summoned top security officials after a Cambodian mortar round hit Thai territory, injuring one soldier. Although Cambodia claimed it was an accident, Anutin emphasized that Cambodia must take full responsibility. He stated that while evacuations are not yet necessary, Thailand is prepared to respond if needed. Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow has already sent a protest letter to Phnom Penh.
title: PM calls security meeting after Cambodian shells land in Thailand, insists Cambodia must take responsibility

summary: The Thai army reported that one soldier was wounded by shrapnel and evacuated for treatment following mortar fire from Cambodian forces on Tuesday morning. While Thailand initially accused Cambodia of a deliberate ceasefire violation, a later statement noted that Cambodian officials contacted a Thai military unit to claim the fire was unintentional. The Thai military has warned that any further incidents could prompt a retaliatory response.
title: Thailand says Cambodia border strike wounds soldier, violates ceasefire

summary: The Ministry of National Defence issued a press release regarding an explosion at 7:27 AM on January 6 in the Mom Bei (Mom 3) area, Preah Vihear. Cambodia states the explosion came from a 'pile of garbage' while troops were cleaning the area, injuring two Cambodian soldiers. The ministry stressed its commitment to the Dec 27 ceasefire and noted that border coordination teams are communicating to resolve the misunderstanding after Thai accusations of mortar fire.
title: Cambodia Clarifies Border Explosion Incident, Reaffirms Full Commitment to Ceasefire

summary: The spokesperson for the Ministry of Interior has issued a formal denial regarding a report by Khaosod English which claimed Thai naval forces seized a Cambodian weapons cache inside a casino building in the Thmor Da area. The Ministry clarified that the building is actually a Cambodian Border Police post located within sovereign Cambodian territory, not a hidden cache, and condemned the report as misinformation.
title: Ministry of Interior denies Khaosod English report on Thai Navy seizing weapon cache

summary: Cambodia has sent a second Note Verbale to Thailand requesting a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting in Siem Reap during the 2nd or 3rd week of January. This follows a postponement by Thailand of a previous request for a meeting in early January. summary: Military delegations from Thailand's 1st Army Area and Cambodia's 5th Military Region met at the Poipet International Border Checkpoint. The two-day session aims to finalize an agenda for high-level Regional Border Committee (RBC) talks scheduled for Thursday. ASEAN observers are present to monitor the proceedings following the Dec 2025 ceasefire agreement.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Begin Border Security Talks Under ASEAN Observation

summary: Prime Minister Anutin stated there is no sign of a third clash with Cambodia. He addressed reports of Cambodia digging trenches, calling it a standard defense tactic. Additionally, he mentioned he has not seen any official documents regarding rumors of Cambodia procuring more air-to-surface or air attack weaponry. He urged the public to live their lives normally as the military has the situation under control.
title: PM Insists Border is Calm, Has Not Seen Leaked Docs on Cambodia Buying Air Weapons

summary: Villagers at the Chong An Ma border in Ubon Ratchathani expressed anxiety over a potential third round of military clashes. They noted that Cambodian forces have been continuously burning grass along the border, which creates smoke that obscures surveillance visibility for Thai observers. While the Thai military maintains the situation is normal, some locals have already prepared their belongings for evacuation, citing past experiences of conflict in the area.
title: Border villagers fear 'Round 3' clash as Cambodians burn grass to mask visibility

summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated there are no indicators of a third round of fighting despite reports of Cambodia digging trenches near the border in Trat. He noted that military units from both sides are communicating regularly to prevent misunderstandings and are adhering to the December 27 ceasefire. Anutin visited Sa Kaeo province to assess the situation and reassured citizens that the government and military have the territory under control.
title: Anutin rules out third round of Thai-Cambodian border clashes

summary: At a UN Security Council debate on the rule of law, Cambodia’s representative accused Thailand of seeking to 'alter the status quo on the ground' and violating international humanitarian law through the targeting of civilians. Thailand responded by stressing that sovereign equality must be upheld in practice, not just rhetoric, subtly accusing Cambodia of not adhering to the law in good faith.
title: Cambodia, Thailand trade veiled barbs at UNSC debate

summary: Analysis suggests the 2025 conflict was driven by Thailand's crackdown on border scam centers and plans to legalize casinos, which threatened Cambodian elite revenue streams, leading to a military escalation.
title: Border crisis exposes Cambodia’s murky political economy

summary: Thai caretaker Deputy PM Anutin Charnvirakul stated there are no signs of a 'third round' of border fighting, proposing joint demining cooperation. However, Cambodian media labels this as 'populist rhetoric' meant to sway voters ahead of the February 8 Thai elections, warning that Cambodian troops remain on high alert due to previous incursions.
title: Anutin declares no third round of border war with Cambodia; Cambodian media remains skeptical

summary: The Royal Thai Navy clarified that the delay in paying allowances to sailors and marines stationed at the Thai-Cambodian border was due to legal processes involving the approval of the central budget. Officials confirmed that the funds have now been transferred and are being disbursed to personnel.
title: Navy explains delay in allowances for Thai-Cambodian border troops

summary: Health Minister Chheang Ra stated during the 45th Health Assembly that the 2025 border conflict with Thailand was a major health crisis, comparable to COVID-19. He reported that Thai military actions destroyed health centers along the border and forced over 500,000 civilians and medical staff to flee to safety zones. The ministry is now working to restore services as displaced persons begin to return to seven border provinces.
title: Health Ministry warns border conflict posed new health threat

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs has officially protested a legal complaint filed in a Thai court by Thailand's National Security Council Secretary-General against Senate President Hun Sen and PM Hun Manet. Cambodia calls the move 'counterproductive' to de-escalation efforts and claims the domestic legal action against foreign leaders has no basis in international law.
title: Cambodia protests against 'hostile action by the Secretary-General of the National Security Council of Thailand directed at the President of the Cambodian Senate and the Prime Minister of Cambodia'

summary: A three-day meeting of the Regional Border Committee (RBC) secretariat held at the Poipet-Aranyaprathet border crossing ended on January 29 without a consensus. Military officials from Cambodia's 5th Military Region and Thailand's 1st Army Area, observed by the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT), agreed to continue exchanging documents and negotiating from their respective headquarters. This follows the December 27 ceasefire after weeks of armed conflict.
title: Cambodia - Thailand meeting over border issues ends with no consensus

summary: Foreign ministers from Southeast Asia met in Cebu, Philippines, for an informal retreat to discuss regional security, including the ongoing Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. Philippine Foreign Minister Ma. Theresa Lazaro emphasized the need for a rules-based approach and restraint. The conflict remains a top priority alongside the Myanmar crisis and South China Sea tensions as the Philippines takes the ASEAN chair for 2026.
title: Philippines hosts ASEAN foreign minister retreat to tackle regional issues

summary: The scheduled signing ceremony between the Thai First Army Commander and the Cambodian 5th Regional Army Commander was canceled. The secretariat-level talks at the Poipet immigration checkpoint failed to resolve outstanding issues. Thai forces remain on high alert to protect sovereignty while waiting for further diplomatic mechanisms to resolve the dispute.
title: RBC meeting collapses! No agreement reached, no signing

summary: During an ASEAN foreign ministers' retreat in Cebu, Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro highlighted the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict as a significant challenge to regional stability. The meeting addressed the 'deadly fighting' that occurred before the US-backed ceasefire in late 2025. Lazaro urged member states to maintain restraint and adhere to international law to preserve peace in the face of growing geopolitical tensions and unilateral actions.
title: ASEAN should adhere to rule of law in face of 'unilateral actions,' Philippines' top diplomat says

Both sides agreed to continue exchanging documents and negotiating from their respective headquarters.
title: Cambodia-Thailand RBC secretariat meeting over border issues concludes with no consensus

title: National News Summary: RBC Meeting between Cambodia-Thailand has not yet found a common center

summary: Military talks between the secretariats of the Regional Border Committee (RBC) representing the Thai First Army Region and the Cambodian 5th Regional Army ended without progress. No joint statement was signed today, though both sides agreed to meet again in the future.
title: Talks between Thai and Cambodian armies end in deadlock

summary: Lt Gen Kanok Netrawatthanasena reported significant defensive preparations, including trenches and bunkers, at disputed border areas like Ta Muen Thom Temple. He argued these movements indicate both sides are positioning for another clash, despite the official ceasefire.
title: Thai ex-deputy commander warns third round of fighting ‘will happen’

summary: The Thai military's Joint Information Centre addressed Cambodian allegations of ceasefire violations between Jan 12-22, 2026. Thailand clarified that its use of drones, installation of temporary barriers, and demining activities were routine security measures within its designated deployment areas and did not violate sovereignty. The statement reaffirmed respect for the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) monitoring the border.
title: Thai military responds to Cambodia’s ceasefire violation claims, reaffirms commitment to GBC guidelines

summary: During the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Retreat in the Philippines, Singapore's Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan urged his Thai counterpart to resolve the border dispute through dialogue. The report highlights that Singapore, usually cautious, has taken a firmer stance following the large-scale clashes in 2025. Cambodian media frames this as Singapore siding with peace and urging Thailand to stop using the border to distract from internal politics.
title: Singapore tells Thailand directly to resolve dispute with Cambodia peacefully

summary: Local reports indicate that Thai forces have been demolishing Cambodian homes and erecting new structures along the border to solidify their presence and obscure previous boundary markers. There is growing public concern and political pressure within Cambodia, with some parties calling for the government to take the case to the International Criminal Court (ICC).
title: Thailand invades, demolishes Cambodian houses and builds new structures to remove traces while Cambodia has yet to sue Thailand

summary: Two Thai soldiers were injured on January 30, 2026, when a grass fire at the Thai-Cambodian border ignited unexploded munitions. The incident was localized and confirmed by military officials to be an accident related to environmental conditions rather than active combat.
title: Thai Soldiers Injured in Border Munition Explosion

summary: The Regional Border Committee (RBC) meeting between Thailand's 1st Army Area and Cambodia's 5th Military Region in Poipet ended without a signed Memorandum of Agreement. Officials stated that while talks were held on January 27-28 to reduce tension, several key points remain unresolved. The Thai Army continues to maintain its sovereignty and troop presence along the border in accordance with the GBC special session statement from late 2025.
title: Thai-Cambodia RBC talks fail to reach agreement; no signing today

summary: A three-day secretariat meeting for the Regional Border Committee (RBC) between Thailand's 1st Army Area and Cambodia's 5th Military Region concluded at Poipet without an agreement. Despite discussions intended to de-escalate tensions following the December ceasefire, the two sides were unable to finalize a memorandum of agreement. Both delegations agreed to return to their headquarters for further internal discussions, though the meeting was described as a positive step for maintaining communication.
title: Thai–Cambodian Border Committee Meeting Ends with No Deal, No Signing

title: RBC Border Talks Fail to Reach Consensus After Two Days of Tense Negotiations

Field visits were conducted on January 20 and 26 to Chong An Ma (Ubon Ratchathani) and Ban Nong Chan (Sa Kaeo) to observe conditions firsthand.
title: Developments on Thai-Cambodian Border Situation, 30 January 2026

summary: The Royal Thai Army has invited the public to participate in a memorial ceremony on February 3, 2026, at the Army Headquarters in Bangkok. The event honors soldiers who died defending Thai sovereignty during the recent armed clashes with Cambodia. The ceremony will include a white rose laying activity and stories of bravery from the front lines.
title: Royal Thai Army to hold memorial for fallen soldiers from border conflict

summary: Thai authorities responded to Cambodian allegations that Thailand violated the ceasefire between January 12 and 22, 2026. Thailand clarified that military actions, including drone use and demining, were conducted strictly for safety and patrolling within Thai territory and do not constitute a violation of sovereignty or the ceasefire agreement. The Thai side urged the use of official channels to resolve doubts rather than public accusations.
title: Thailand Rejects Cambodian Accusations of Ceasefire Violations, Vows Adherence to GBC Framework

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFAIC) expressed 'serious concern' after Thai National Security Council Secretary-General Chatchai Bangchuad reportedly filed a police report seeking the arrest of Cambodia's top leadership. The Ministry called the action inconsistent with the ASEAN Charter and international principles regarding the immunity of state leaders, labeling it a move that 'adds heat' to the border situation instead of cooling it down.
title: Cambodia Protests Thai NSC Attempt to Arrest Top Leaders

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated that legal complaints filed in Thai courts against Senate President Hun Sen and PM Hun Manet regarding 2025 military operations are 'baseless' under international law. He argued these moves contradict the spirit of the December 2025 Joint Declaration and threaten the current ceasefire. The Cambodian government views these legal actions as a provocation that hinders the restoration of normal bilateral relations.
title: Government Spokesman Says Thai Legal Complaints Undermine Border Peace

summary: Following the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Retreat in Cebu, geopolitical analysts in Cambodia are optimistic that the Philippines, as the 2026 ASEAN Chair, will prioritize the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. Experts hope that the 'Journey Toward a Shared Future' theme will lead to concrete mechanisms for resolving the dispute through international law and peaceful dialogue, reducing the military tension seen in recent months.
title: Experts Expect Philippines to Mediate Border Dispute as New ASEAN Chair

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) expressed disappointment over Cambodia's continued use of 'distorted rhetoric' and fake news. The deputy spokesperson emphasized that Thailand is strictly following the joint statement from the December ceasefire. Thailand has established a 'Joint Information Center' to provide accurate facts and counter fake news. The MFA also rejected claims that Thailand denied visas to certain Cambodian officials, calling such reports groundless and unhelpful for de-escalation.
title: MFA Disappointed by Cambodia's Continued 'Distorted Rhetoric' Aimed at Damaging Thailand's Image

The party suggested using international alliances to pressure Cambodia into cooperation on human trafficking and financial crimes. This stance comes as Thai political parties prepare for the February snap election, with border security and relations with neighbors becoming central campaign issues.
title: Pheu Thai Outlines '3D Diplomacy' to Surround Cambodia with Global Pressure to Stop Scammers

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn told ASEAN ministers in Cebu that while Cambodia remains committed to the December 27 ceasefire, certain 'actions' (referring to Thai military moves) continue to violate Cambodian sovereignty and territorial integrity. He emphasized that tens of thousands of Cambodian civilians still cannot return home because their houses are blocked by barriers or have been destroyed. He thanked Malaysia for its previous mediation but urged the new chair to maintain pressure for a peaceful solution.
title: Cambodian Foreign Minister Calls on ASEAN to Support Border Solution Amid Ceasefire Violations

summary: On the night of Jan 30, sounds of 40mm grenade launchers and laser sightings were reported near Phupa Lek, Si Sa Ket. Thai forces fired warning shots. Commanders from both sides coordinated to resolve the issue, which was initially attributed to a lack of discipline among Cambodian local troops (Tachapana) rather than a planned attack.
title: Army Region 2 updates border situation: 40mm grenade launcher sounds heard in Kantharalak, Si Sa Ket

summary: The Chinese government has delivered the first of two planned aid shipments to Thailand, totaling 10 million yuan in value. The supplies, including blankets, folding beds, and winter clothes, are intended for Thai civilians living along the border who have been affected by the recent conflict. The delivery was received at Suvarnabhumi Airport by the Thai Minister of Defense on behalf of Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul.
title: China Sends Humanitarian Aid to Thailand for Distribution to Civilians at Thai-Cambodian Border

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul addressed reports of recent border unrest, stating that while the situation has been cleared, Cambodia should not allow such incidents to happen frequently. He emphasized that the Thai military is strong and dismissed claims that the tension was being used as a tool for political campaigning ahead of the upcoming election.
title: PM Warns Cambodia Not to 'Repeat' Border Unrest, Denies Campaign Link

summary: The State Secretariat of Border Affairs issued a firm protest against Thai military actions, including the clearing of Cambodian homes and preventing citizens from returning to their residences. Cambodia has proposed a new timeline (Feb 9-13) for joint survey teams to resume border marking to prevent further unilateral changes to the landscape.
title: Cambodia Protests Thai Military Destruction of Houses and Blocking of Returnees

summary: At the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Retreat in Cebu, Philippines, Cambodia's Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn briefed counterparts on the border conflict. ASEAN ministers issued a collective commitment to uphold regional peace and urged the full implementation of the December 27, 2025, ceasefire agreement. The meeting emphasized the role of the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) in verifying agreed de-escalation measures.
title: ASEAN ministers back peaceful end to Cambodia-Thailand border tensions

summary: Thai authorities assisted 32 Thai citizens in escaping a scam compound in Cambodia. Victims revealed they were tortured if they failed to meet targets and were threatened with having their organs harvested. They managed to flee during a building raid on January 17 and sought help at the Thai embassy in Phnom Penh.
title: 32 Thais Rescued from Cambodian Call Center Scams

summary: Thai Marines arrested seven Chinese nationals attempting to enter Thailand illegally via natural border crossings in Chanthaburi. The suspects carried dozens of phones and Cambodian SIM cards, likely linked to scam operations. During border security operations, the Thai military reportedly fired warning shots after a security alarm was triggered, highlighting the high state of alert along the frontier.
title: Seven Chinese scam suspects arrested in Chanthaburi province

summary: Gen. Boonsin Padklang visited Surin province to pay respects at Prasat Ta Muean Thom and other ancient sites. He confirmed that despite recent clashes where explosives landed near military bases, the main Buddha statues at these sites remained undamaged, serving as a morale boost for troops.
title: Army Advisor Visits Border Temples, Confirms Sacred Sites Unharmed

summary: Thai media reported that Cambodian forces allegedly fired M-79 grenades at Phu Pha Lek, prompting the 2nd Army Region to retaliate. The report uses strong nationalist language, accusing the other side of 'playing unfair' during a period of fragile relations.
title: Alleged M-79 Attack at Phu Pha Lek; Thai Army Retaliates
